questions.question: In computer architecture, what defines the interface between software and hardware, specifying the set of instructions a processor can execute, its registers, and memory models, without detailing its internal implementation?
options: Microarchitecture
Physical Design
Instruction Set Architecture (ISA)
Register Transfer Level (RTL)
System-on-Chip (SoC)

questions.question: In a pipelined processor, which type of hazard occurs when two or more instructions require the same hardware resource at the same time, such as two instructions trying to use the same memory port or functional unit in the same clock cycle?
options: Data Hazard
Control Hazard
Structural Hazard
Memory Hazard
Latency Hazard

questions.question: During the post-silicon validation phase of an integrated circuit, what is the primary purpose of 'Shmoo Plotting'?
options: To generate the final GDSII layout for tape-out.
To identify and characterize the operating voltage and frequency limits of the chip.
To perform Static Timing Analysis (STA) on the fabricated silicon.
To verify the correctness of the logical design against the RTL specification.
To simulate parasitic capacitance and resistance post-layout extraction.

questions.question: In the physical verification stage of digital IC design, what is the primary objective of 'Layout Versus Schematic' (LVS) checking?
options: To verify that all transistors meet the minimum size requirements specified by design rules.
To ensure that the physical layout accurately represents the intended logical netlist.
To identify manufacturing defects on the fabricated silicon die.
To analyze the power consumption of the entire chip layout.
To optimize the placement of standard cells for better timing.

questions.question: In digital circuits, what is the primary function of a decoder?
options: To convert multiple input lines into a single output line, based on a select signal.
To convert a binary input code into a unique active output line.
To store a single bit of information and maintain its state.
To combine multiple input signals into a single output using a logical AND operation.
To amplify an analog signal for digital processing.
